paras: The attempted lynching of Jack Hemphill took place at Gainesville, Georgia, on a Friday night in November 1888, when a crowd gathered to lynch Hemphill, a Black man held in the town lock-up. The marshal reached the lock-up ahead of the crowd and spirited the prisoner away, and no one was reported hurt.

Hemphill, described as "colored," was arrested that Friday night on a charge of "attempting an outrage on a white girl of 12 years" and placed in the lock-up. The report names neither the girl nor any witness, and it gives no account of the alleged offense beyond the charge.

After the arrest, according to the only report found, "a crowd gathered and started to lynch him." The marshal "beat the crowd to the lock-up," took Hemphill out and "spirited him away." The size of the crowd, the names of any of its members and the place to which Hemphill was taken are not reported.
No report of a trial, of any arrests in the crowd, or of what became of Hemphill was found, and the one surviving account breaks off in mid-word.

The episode is known from a single paragraph in the Savannah Morning News of Sunday, November 11, 1888, printed on page 6 in its column "Georgia and Florida. News of the Two States Told in Paragraphs." It followed an item on a town incorporation scheme from the Montezuma Record, and it stated the charge and the crowd's purpose without comment on either. Like other items in the column, it marked the race of the accused, "colored," and of the girl, "white."
No other newspaper's version and no local Gainesville report of the episode was found.

bases: A crowd gathered and 'started to lynch' a prisoner in the Gainesville lock-up, and the marshal removed him before it reached him [A1].
The only report says a crowd started to lynch Hemphill over an accusation of attempted outrage but the marshal took him away first, so no one was killed; this was an attempted lynching [A1].
One brief paragraph in the Savannah Morning News is the only report found [A1].

accounts.label: Savannah Morning News state-news paragraph
accounts.gist: Hemphill was arrested for attempting an outrage on a 12-year-old white girl; a crowd started to lynch him, but the marshal got to the lock-up first and spirited him away.

framing.detail: A three-sentence item in the column 'Georgia and Florida. News of the Two States Told in Paragraphs', stating the accusation as the cause of arrest and the crowd's aim without comment on either.

No county is named; Hall is an inference from Gainesville under the column's Georgia subheading.
The paper reports only that a crowd gathered and started to lynch him and that the marshal reached the lock-up first; no siege of the lock-up is described.
